title: "Information Retrieval Textual — Revision"
---

# Model Bag of Words

**Principle**: terms = independent, unordered entities, multiplicity

| Advantage | Disadvantage |
|---|---|
| Simple, generic (text, images...) | Loss of grammatical structure |
| No need for full TAL | Unmanaged Synonymy / Polysaemia |
| Light, computable | Order of words ignored |

**Term** = generic entity (word, visual pattern, acoustic pattern...)

---

# Text Processing Pipeline

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    A[Gross document] --> B[Tokenization]
    B --> C[Stopwords removal]
    C --> D[Stemming / Lemmatization]
    D --> E[Index / Thesaurus]
```

| Step | Role | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Tokenization** | Bytes → tokens | separators: spaces, punctuation |
| **Stopwords** | Delete non-discriminatory terms | *"the"*, *"a"*, *"of"* |
| **Stemming** | Root of the word (truncated) | *committed* → *commit* |
| **Lammatization** | Basic language form | *"are"*, *"is"* → *"be"* |
| **SOUNDEX** | Phonetic key 4 characters | *Herman* → **H655** |

**Stemming vs Lemmatization**: Stemming = faster but less accurate; lemmatization = linguistically correct

# Zipf's Law

**Class definition** $r(i)$: position in list sorted by decreasing frequency

$$\boxed{f(i) \cdot r(i) = K \approx \text{cst}} \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad f(i) = \frac{KL}{r(i)}, \quad K \approx 0.1$$

**Loi de puissance** (power law) avec $c = -1$ → **droite en log-log**

$$\log f(i) = \log(KL) - \log(r(i))$$

## Prediction of the number of terms

$$s_n = r_n - r_{n+1} = \frac{KL}{n(n+1)} \qquad \frac{s_n}{M} = \frac{1}{n(n+1)}$$

| n (occurrences) | Fraction prédite | Fraction réelle (TREC) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 (hapax) | **0.500** | 0.402 |
| 2 | 0.167 | 0.132 |
| 5 | 0.033 | 0.032 |

⚠️ **Moitié des termes distincts n'apparaissent qu'une seule fois** (hapax legomena)

## Correction de Mandelbrot

$$f(i) = P(r(i) + \rho)^{-B}, \quad P=10^{5.4},\ \rho=100,\ B=1.15$$

Improves fit to extreme ranks

## Practical consequences

- Stopwords removal → greatly reduces storage
- Rare terms → unreliable statistics

---

# Heap's Law

$$\boxed{M = k \cdot L^{\beta}}, \quad k \approx 10\text{–}100,\quad \beta \approx 0.4\text{–}0.6$$

- $M$ = taille du vocabulaire, $L$ = longueur du corpus (tokens)
- $\beta \approx 0.5$ → $M \propto \sqrt{L}$ (croissance **sous-linéaire**)
- Dérivable depuis la loi de Zipf

⚠️ Vocabulaire non borné (entités nommées, fautes…)

---

# Vocabulaire d'Index selon Luhn

- **Seuil supérieur** (Upper Cut-Off) → élimine les stopwords (trop fréquents)
- **Seuil inférieur** (Lower Cut-Off) → élimine les hapax (trop rares)
- **Termes significatifs** = zone intermédiaire à haute valeur discriminante

---

# Théorie de l'Information

## Entropie

$$I_H(T) = -\sum_{i=1}^{M} p_i \log p_i \quad \text{(max si équiprobable)}$$

| Vocabulary M | Real entropy | Max entropy |
|---|---|---|
| 100 000 | 9.5 bits | 13.3 bits |
| 500,000 | 10.9 bits | 15.6 bits |
| 1 000 000 | 11.4 bits | 16.6 bits |

## Mutual Information

$$I(W_1;W_2) = \sum_{w_1,w_2} \mathbb{P}(w_1,w_2)\log\frac{\mathbb{P}(w_1,w_2)}{\mathbb{P}(w_1)\mathbb{P}(w_2)}$$

| Valeur | Interprétation |
|---|---|
| Grande | Co-occurrence **significative** |
| Proche de 0 | Co-occurrence **spurieuse** (termes fréquents) |

⚠️ Pièges : termes très fréquents (*"a"*, *"is"*, *"with"*) → IM artificiellement élevée → stopwords à supprimer

# Formules à Retenir

| Formule | Nom | Variables |
|---|---|---|
| $f(i) \cdot r(i) = K$ | Zipf | $f$ = fréquence, $r$ = rang |
| $f(i) = KL/r(i)$, $K\approx0.1$ | Zipf développée | $L$ = longueur corpus |
| $s_n/M = 1/n(n+1)$ | Fraction hapax | $s_n$ = termes à $n$ occurrences |
| $M = k \cdot L^\beta$ | Heap | $M$ = vocab, $\beta \in [0.4, 0.6]$ |
| $I_H = -\sum p_i \log p_i$ | Entropie Shannon | $p_i$ = proba du terme $i$ |
| $f(i) = P(r+\rho)^{-B}$ | Mandelbrot | $P, \rho, B$ = constantes empiriques |
